definitions.gloss: vigorously; forcefully; with great energy; with momentum
definitions.explanation: Doing something with strong force, speed, or enthusiasm. Describes energetic, dynamic movement or action.

examples.japanese: {水|みず}が{勢|いきお}いよく{流|なが}れている。
{子|こ}どもたちが{勢|いきお}いよく{走|はし}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: The children dashed out with great energy.

examples.japanese: ドアを{勢|いきお}いよく{開|あ}けたら、{壁|かべ}にぶつかってしまった。
examples.english: I opened the door forcefully and it slammed into the wall.

notes:
The adverbial form of {勢|いきお}いがよい (having momentum/force). {勢|いきお}い is a noun meaning "momentum, force, vigor," and よく is the adverbial form of よい (good). Together they describe an action performed with noticeable force or energy.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {勢|いきお}いよく{飛|と}び{出|だ}す — to jump out energetically
- {勢|いきお}いよく{流|なが}れる — to flow strongly
- {勢|いきお}いよく{食|た}べる — to eat with gusto
- {勢|いきお}いよく{成長|せいちょう}する — to grow vigorously

SIMILAR ADVERBS:
- {激|はげ}しく — violently, intensely (stronger; implies more extreme force)
- {力強|ちからづよ}く — powerfully, strongly (focuses on strength)
- {元気|げんき}よく — cheerfully, energetically (focuses on liveliness rather than physical force)
- {一気|いっき}に — all at once (focuses on speed and continuity rather than force)
